scope: Enforce the official German IdNr leading-zero and first-ten-digit repetition rules while preserving MOD 11,10 behavior and prior J1/J2 regressions.
authorization_basis: The user directed implementation and focused re-audit of repaired sections one by one and explicitly directed continuation to the other high-probability sections.

changes.change: Reject a leading zero and require exactly one repeated digit occurring two or three times among the first ten digits before applying the unchanged MOD 11,10 calculation.
Apply the same minimal validator change; active scanner copies remain byte-identical.
Add three conventional assertion groups for valid, structurally invalid, leading-zero, and wrong-checksum values.
Correct only the temporary golden-test Steuer-ID generator so its generated positive controls satisfy the official repetition rule; the historical golden program remains unchanged.

failed_groups: checksum-valid but structurally invalid values were detected as valid
leading-zero value was detected as valid

preintegration_quality_gate.initial_observation: The corrected validator caused the unchanged J1 golden generator to produce 20 structurally invalid positive controls, so the golden positive test failed while the allow-all mutation still passed.
preintegration_quality_gate.resolution: Integrated the already reviewed J3 test-only generator correction from the Janis receipt, without changing the historical golden program.
preintegration_quality_gate.mutation_result: Removing the new leading-zero/repetition guard recreated exactly two J3 assertion-group failures while official structurally valid controls still passed.

limitations: This receipt is remediation validation, not a controller-sealed L1-A19 audit verdict.
The current scanner hash supersedes R11's hash-bound L1-A18 target; R11 remains immutable historical evidence, and the L1-A19 audit must retain L1-A18 regressions as controls.
No live Docker container, service restart, external deployment identity, or overall WPNO status was tested.
